scams.title: Airport Taxi Tout Overcharge
scams.description: Unlicensed taxi touts intercept arrivals before the prepaid counter and quote ₹800–1,200 for a trip to Paltan Bazaar. The fair rate is ₹300–380.
scams.howToAvoid: Walk past all touts to the prepaid taxi counter inside the terminal. Fixed rate to city centre is ~₹350. Ola/Uber also available once outside.
redFlags: Approaches you before you reach the exit

scams.title: Fake Priest VIP Darshan
scams.description: Men in saffron robes outside the temple offer 'VIP darshan' bypassing the queue for ₹2,000–5,000. They pocket the money and either vanish or lead you to an unrelated private house.
scams.howToAvoid: VIP darshan tickets are sold only at the official temple trust counter at the gate. No legitimate priest solicits outside.

scams.title: Auto-Rickshaw Tampered Meter
scams.description: Autos in Paltan Bazaar use meters calibrated to run 1.5–2× faster than the legal rate. Short trips of 2–3 km end up costing ₹150–200 instead of ₹50–80.
scams.howToAvoid: Agree on a fixed price before boarding. Standard rate is ₹10–12/km. For trips under 3 km, ₹50–80 is typical.
redFlags: Refuses to quote a fixed price

scams.title: Fake Porter Baggage Fee
scams.description: Unofficial porters grab luggage without quoting a price, carry it 20 metres to the exit, then demand ₹300–500. Licensed porters charge ₹30–50 per bag and wear a red uniform with an ID badge.
scams.howToAvoid: Only engage porters wearing red uniforms with visible Railway badge. Agree on the fee before handing over bags.
redFlags: Demands payment before you can leave

scams.title: Silk & Handicraft Quality Fraud
scams.description: Shops targeting tourists sell synthetic fabric labelled as Assam silk (muga/eri) at genuine silk prices of ₹2,000–8,000 per metre. The cloth is indistinguishable to untrained eyes.
scams.howToAvoid: Buy silk only from Assam Silk stores with GI-tag certification or the Government Silk Emporium on G.S. Road. Rub the fabric — real silk warms quickly.
redFlags: Shop has no GI certification displayed

scams.title: Boat Ride Hidden Charges
scams.description: Boatmen quote ₹100–150 for a Brahmaputra river crossing or sunset cruise, then add charges mid-trip for 'island entry', 'life jacket fee', and 'guide fee' totalling ₹400–600.
scams.howToAvoid: Ask explicitly before boarding: 'Is this the total price, no extra charges?' Government ASTC ferries have fixed printed fares. Agree on an all-inclusive price.

scams.title: Tourist Taxi Price Inflation
scams.description: Drivers at Police Bazaar quote out-of-state tourists 50–100% above local rates. Cherrapunji return (which locals pay ₹1,200) is quoted at ₹2,500–3,500.
scams.howToAvoid: Fair rate: Cherrapunji return ₹1,200–1,800. Ask your hotel to arrange a car or compare with at least two other drivers. Ola is available in Shillong.
redFlags: Quotes significantly higher than hotel estimate
Won't share cab with other passengers

scams.title: Airport Cab Monopoly Pricing
scams.description: The 35 km Umroi Airport to Police Bazaar route is quoted at ₹1,500–2,000 by unregulated cabs. The official prepaid rate is ₹700–900.
scams.howToAvoid: Use the prepaid taxi counter at the arrivals exit. Confirm the price is ₹800 or less before moving to the vehicle.
redFlags: Starts driving before agreeing on price

scams.title: Fake Waterfall Entry Tickets
scams.description: Unofficial ticket sellers near Nohkalikai Falls and Seven Sisters Falls charge ₹150–300 entry. The actual Forest Department rate is ₹20–40 per person.
scams.howToAvoid: Only buy tickets from the official forest department kiosk at the main gate. It has a printed rate chart. Never buy from individuals on the road.
redFlags: Selling tickets away from the main gate

scams.title: Unofficial Village Guide Overcharge
scams.description: Self-appointed guides at the 'Cleanest Village in Asia' charge ₹500–1,000 for a walk that takes 20 minutes and needs no guide. The village is tiny and well-signed.
scams.howToAvoid: Mawlynnong is easy to navigate independently. If you want a guide, the community-run visitor centre charges a fair ₹100–200.

scams.title: Hotel 'Government Approved' Scam
scams.description: Touts near the bus stand steer tourists to specific hotels claiming they are 'government approved' or 'tourist department certified' and earn commission. These hotels are often overpriced or substandard.
scams.howToAvoid: Book accommodation in advance through reputable platforms. Ignore unsolicited hotel recommendations from strangers at bus/taxi stands.

scams.title: Unofficial Parking & Entry Fee
scams.description: Locals near Laitlum collect ₹100–200 'parking fees' and ₹50 per person 'entry fees' that have no official basis. The area is a community-managed viewpoint with nominal or no entry charge.
scams.howToAvoid: Ask for an official receipt. The legitimate community fee (if any) is ₹20–30 per person. Refuse to pay without a proper receipt.

scams.title: Tsomgo + Nathula Package Inflation
scams.description: Travel agents on MG Marg quote ₹5,000–8,000 per car for Tsomgo Lake + Nathula. The fair rate including permits is ₹2,500–3,500. Agents claim inflated 'processing fees' for permits that cost nothing extra.
scams.howToAvoid: Book permits directly at the Tourism & Civil Aviation Dept office. Compare at least 3 agents. Fair private cab rate is ₹2,800–3,200 for both sites.

scams.title: Bagdogra to Gangtok Overcharge
scams.description: Touts at Bagdogra quote ₹4,000–5,000 for a private cab to Gangtok. Shared taxis from the official stand cost ₹300–350 per seat; private cab fair rate is ₹2,200–2,800.
scams.howToAvoid: Head to the official shared taxi stand outside arrivals. For private cab, use pre-booked services or confirm the rate is under ₹2,800 before departure.
redFlags: Intercepts before you reach the taxi stand

scams.title: Fake Monastery Guide
scams.description: Unlicensed guides outside Rumtek and Enchey Monastery offer 'exclusive inner sanctum' access for ₹800–2,000. No such access exists for tourists; they simply walk you around the public courtyard.
scams.howToAvoid: Monastery entry is free or has a small donation box. Government-licensed guides carry a laminated Tourism Dept ID card. Pay no more than ₹400–600 for a half-day guide.

scams.title: Organic Sikkim Product Mislabelling
scams.description: Shops sell generic tea, cardamom, and honey labelled as 'certified organic Sikkim' at 3–5× the price of identical products from Darjeeling or Nepal. The 'organic' certification is often a printed sticker with no verification.
scams.howToAvoid: Buy certified organic Sikkim products from the Sikkim Organic Mission outlet at MG Marg or the State Government Emporium. Ask for the certification number.
redFlags: Sold only to tourists, not locals

scams.title: Hidden Hotel Tax & Service Charge
scams.description: Budget guesthouses add 'tourism cess', 'room service charge', and 'heater fee' to the bill that were not mentioned at check-in, inflating the bill by 20–35%.
scams.howToAvoid: Ask at check-in for a full breakdown of all charges. Request a written quote. GST is standard (12–18%) but additional local cess or 'heater fee' should be negotiated upfront.
redFlags: Bill significantly higher than quoted price

scams.title: Nathula Permit Middleman
scams.description: Agents near the Tourism Office charge ₹300–600 as 'facilitation fees' to process Nathula permits. The permit itself is free and can be obtained directly at the SDM office with your documents.
scams.howToAvoid: Bring original ID, passport photos, and vehicle registration to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) office. Processing is free. Your hotel can guide you.
redFlags: Asks for original documents to keep
Works from an unofficial-looking office near the govt building

scams.title: Bumla Pass Permit Fraud
scams.description: Agents near Tawang town collect ₹500–1,000 per person for Bumla Pass permits that are completely free. They claim 'special government processing' is required.
scams.howToAvoid: Bumla permits are obtained free at the DC (Deputy Commissioner) office in Tawang with your ILP and passport. No agent is needed. Your hotel can accompany you.
redFlags: Operates from a roadside desk near the DC office

scams.title: Fake Photography Permit
scams.description: Individuals at Sela Lake and the pass viewpoint demand ₹200–500 for a 'photography permit'. No such permit exists. This is entirely fraudulent.
scams.howToAvoid: There is no photography fee at Sela Pass. Refuse politely and walk away. If aggressive, note the person's description and report to the nearest ITBP post.
redFlags: Demands cash before you take a photo
Amount changes when you question it

scams.title: Mid-Route Fare Revision
scams.description: Hired drivers on the Tezpur–Tawang route claim road closures, military checkpoints, or 'extra fuel costs' mid-journey to demand ₹500–1,500 above the agreed fare.
scams.howToAvoid: Fix the fare in writing on a signed paper before departure. Clarify: 'This price is final regardless of road conditions.' Use hotel-recommended drivers only.
redFlags: Mentions road problems shortly after departure
Stops at a dhaba and 'discusses' costs
Says he needs extra for 'toll' on a free road

scams.title: Monastery Souvenir Price Gouging
scams.description: Souvenir stalls inside and around Tawang Monastery sell thangka paintings, prayer flags, and singing bowls at 3–10× their actual value, targeting foreign and domestic tourists equally.
scams.howToAvoid: Compare prices at the local market in Tawang town (10 min walk). Singing bowls: ₹300–500 fair; prayer flags: ₹30–80 per string. Bargain confidently.
redFlags: Price drops dramatically when you hesitate

scams.title: ILP Facilitation Fee Scam
scams.description: Agents near transport hubs charge ₹300–800 to 'arrange' Inner Line Permits for Arunachal Pradesh. ILPs are free and can be obtained online at the Arunachal online portal or at any DC/SDM office.
scams.howToAvoid: Apply online at arunachalipr.gov.in (free) or at the DC/SDM office in person. No agent needed. Carry printout of your ILP at all times.
redFlags: Asks for money before showing you the process
Works outside the government office building

scams.title: Unofficial Jeep Safari Tickets
scams.description: Touts sell jeep safari tickets outside the gate for ₹2,000–3,000 per person. Official Forest Dept jeep safari is ₹700–900 per seat including park entry.
scams.howToAvoid: Book only at official counters inside the gate (Kohora, Bagori, Agaratoli ranges). Carry original ID. Online booking available at kaziranga.nic.in.
redFlags: Ticket has no Forest Dept stamp

scams.title: Resort Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Resort-arranged taxis to Jorhat or Furkating charge ₹1,500–2,000 for routes that cost locals ₹700–900. Resorts add an undisclosed commission.
scams.howToAvoid: Ask the resort to call a local taxi directly, not through their 'partner'. Fair rate: Jorhat ₹800–1,000, Furkating ₹500–600, Guwahati shared cab ₹300/seat.
redFlags: Driver is unfamiliar with local fares

scams.title: Fake Wildlife Guide Certification
scams.description: Guides without Assam Forest Department certification pose as licensed wildlife naturalists, charging ₹1,500–2,500/day for a service a certified guide provides for ₹600–800.
scams.howToAvoid: Ask to see the green Assam Forest Department guide badge with photo ID. Book through the official guide counter at the park gate. Certified guides also know animal locations better.

scams.title: Elephant Safari Hidden Charges
scams.description: Touts for elephant safaris quote ₹400–500 per person then add 'mahout tip', 'camera fee', 'insurance', and 'park contribution' to charge ₹900–1,200 total.
scams.howToAvoid: Elephant safaris are ₹900–1,200 all-inclusive when booked at the official Forest Dept counter. All charges should be on the receipt. Tip the mahout separately at your discretion (₹50–100).
redFlags: Fees added after you've mounted the elephant
No printed receipt for each charge

scams.title: Roadside Restaurant Tourist Menu
scams.description: Roadside dhabas near the park hand tourists a separate 'tourist menu' with prices 2–3× the regular menu. A thali that costs locals ₹80–100 is charged at ₹200–300.
scams.howToAvoid: Ask to see the regular menu or ask other diners what they paid. A full Assamese thali should cost ₹80–150 anywhere along NH-37.
redFlags: Menu brought out only after seeing you're a tourist
No prices on the board outside
Staff hesitant to quote price before ordering
